concept.name: Point of control
concept.definition: The price level with the greatest number of TPOs in a Market Profile — the longest row of the distribution, conventionally taken closest to the center of the range. It is interpreted as the session's fairest price: the level where the market spent the most time and, in Dalton's phrase, the fairest price at which to trade.
concept.intuition: The POC is the price the market kept coming back to — the session's center of gravity.
concept.mechanics: Identified directly from the finished or developing profile as the price row with the most TPO letters (in volume profiles, the row with the most traded volume); migrating POCs during a session indicate directional value discovery.
concept.failure_modes: On trend days the distribution is elongated and the POC is nearly meaningless; prior-session POCs exert no magnetic force in themselves — they are reference levels whose usefulness depends entirely on context.
concept.misconceptions: The POC is not a proven magnet or a guaranteed support/resistance line; it is a descriptive statistic of where time was spent, and treating it as predictive is a misuse of the framework.
concept.example: The widest TPO row of the session sits at 4,520; when price opens at 4,533 the next day and rotates back, traders watch 4,520 as the reference for whether the market re-accepts yesterday's value.
